arguments.distinguishes: It separates plan-level truncation (truncated effective_horizon plus User_Requested_Stop budget stops) from actuator/force saturation (tensions pinned near 8 N): truncated horizons and budget stops with sub-limit tensions would retain solver.terminal_horizon_truncation and controller.budget_truncated_plan_selection while weakening tendon_force_limit_saturation_driving_hold_speed; full 10-interval horizons or near-limit tensions would reverse those two effects. The retained scalar comparisons alone cannot separate these mechanisms, since terminal reach passes while both holding limits fail.

expected.observation: For the queried late run-up and settling-window updates the archived plans view returns effective_horizon below the configured 10 intervals (e.g., 5), continuing the update-30 truncation.
For the queried updates the archived plans view returns optimization_raw_status = User_Requested_Stop with optimization_selected_iteration = 0.
For the queried updates actual_tension_n remains a clear margin below the 8.0 N per-tendon limit rather than pinned at saturation.

limitations: Plans-view records are controller-update evidence, not backend motion, and cannot by themselves establish that any plan truncation, budget stop or tension level caused the sampled holding-window violation.
Only the selected update_ids (at most 8 of 35) are covered; the remaining updates stay not_read rather than inferred absent.
No continuous-time guarantee; the holding window is 6 samples over 0.05 s and the speed signal is a Jacobian-reconstructed norm, not finite differencing.
Read-only retained-evidence query: no numerical solve, no backend execution, and no causal attribution; terminal reach success is compatible with holding speed failure.
missing_information: Per-update effective_horizon, optimization_raw_status, optimization_selected_iteration and actual_tension_n for the 27 updates not previously displayed (only 0,5,10,15,20,25,30,34 were shown), specifically the late run-up and settling window.
No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability exists to confirm that any truncation, budget stop or tension value actually caused the sampled holding-window violation.
arguments.question: For a spread of controller updates not yet displayed (the settling window and its run-up), does the archived plans view show per-update effective_horizon truncated below the configured 10 intervals together with budget-driven optimization stops, rather than per-tendon tensions pinned near the 8 N limit, so as to distinguish plan-truncation explanations from a tendon force-saturation explanation of the sampled holding-window position/speed violation?

relationships.relevance: Nearly every update stops by User_Requested_Stop (F507 = 34) rather than convergence (Solve_Succeeded F466 = 1; Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded F528 = 1), while mean complete-update time F458 = 17.77877309145406 s dwarfs the 0.01 s control period F521 = 0.01 s, so plan selection plausibly runs out of its allotted solve budget at most updates.

Two sampled updates record effective_horizon = 10 intervals (F468 for update 2, F472 for update 0) equal to the configured horizon F502 = 10, so the sampled record does not show run-wide truncation; only one late update was reported truncated, leaving this hypothesis unresolved and testable on the unread settling-window updates.

Both runs record force_bound_violation_n = 0.0 (F379 candidate, F420 baseline), so the per-tendon 8 N bound is not recorded as violated, which weighs against force-limit saturation as the driver; per-update actual_tension_n proximity to the limit is still unread.

stopping_conditions: Stop after the single plans-view batch returns effective_horizon, optimization_raw_status, optimization_selected_iteration and actual_tension_n for the selected update_ids.
Conclude if the returned horizon, stop reason, selected iteration and applied tensions do not co-vary with the recorded settling-window violation.
Do not exceed one read or 180 s wall; do not extend to unlisted update_ids or to numerical solves in this check.
